feeds.title: The Housing Bubble Blog
feeds.description: The Housing Bubble Blog by Ben Jones examines the home price boom and its effect on owners, lenders, regulators, realtors and the economy as a whole.

feeds.title: Wolf Street » Housing
feeds.description: Wolf Richter, publisher of Wolf Street provides the stories about economic, business, and financial issues, Wall Street shenanigans, complex entanglements, and other things, debacles, and opportunities that catches his eye in the US, Europe, Japan, and occasionally China.

feeds.title: Bubbleinfo
feeds.description: Bubbleinfo documents the trends in North SD County coastal real estate by Jim Klinge, broker associated with Compass. In 2005, it became obvious to us that a real estate bubble was forming, so Jim began documenting the local real estate market conditions for our clients. It's a free and easy resource to learn about the market, and to get a feel for how we can help you - we want to be your realtor!

feeds.title: Dr. Housing Bubble
feeds.description: Dr. Housing Bubble Blog provides a candid account of what is going on in today's housing market. It covers topics such as regional housing, California real estate, UK housing bubble, housing chronicles, housing panic, housing wire, and more.

feeds.title: Seattle Bubble Blog
feeds.description: Seattle Bubble is the Seattle area's #1 resource for news, analysis, commentary, and community discussion on the local real estate market. It discusses articles on economy, neighborhoods, features, opinions, polls, and more.

feeds.title: Sacramento Appraisal Blog » Real Estate Bubble
feeds.description: The Sacramento Appraisal Blog is a top-ranking appraisal blog and it exists to help illuminate the local housing market in the greater Sacramento area as well as a resource to the real estate community and the general public on how to understand the appraisal process and better work with appraisers. The site includes real estate bubble articles in the field of bankruptcy, property taxes, estate settlement and more.
